title: The Ploughman, the Ass, and the Ox
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Ploughman yoked his Ox and his Ass together, and set to work to plough his field. It was a poor makeshift of a team, but it was the best he could do, as he had but a single Ox. At the end of the day, when the beasts were loosed from the yoke, the Ass said to the Ox, "Well, we've had a hard day: which of us is to carry the master home?" The Ox looked surprised at the question. "Why," said he, "you, to be sure, as usual."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what two animals did the Ploughman yoke together?
options: His Ox and his Ass
Two Oxen he had borrowed
An Ass and a Horse
Two Asses from his neighbour

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Ploughman set the team to do?
options: Plough his field
Carry water from the well
Pull a cart of grain to market
Turn a mill wheel

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why did the Ploughman use this particular team, despite calling it a poor makeshift?
options: He had but a single Ox
He wanted to train the Ass for future work
The Ox was too old to work alone
He could not afford to buy any oxen at all

questions.prompt: According to the passage, when did the Ass ask the Ox about carrying the master home?
options: When the beasts were loosed from the yoke at the end of the day
As soon as the ploughing began that morning
While they were still yoked together in the field
The following morning before work resumed

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what question does the Ass ask the Ox?
options: Which of us is to carry the master home
Which of us worked harder today
Who deserves to rest first tonight
Whether the master will feed them well

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Ox react to the Ass's question?
options: He looks surprised at the question
He laughs at the Ass for asking
He refuses to answer at all
He argues that the Ass should carry the master

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why is the Ox surprised by the Ass's question?
options: Carrying the master home is plainly always the Ass's task, so the answer seems obvious to him
He did not expect the Ass to speak to him at all
He thought the Ass wanted to carry him instead
He believed the master no longer needed to be carried

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable, given the Ass's question and the Ox's reply?
options: Some burdens fall on one party regardless of how the work was actually shared
Oxen are always stronger than asses in every task
Ploughmen should never yoke two different kinds of animals together
Asses should refuse to carry their masters home

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the passage describe the team of Ox and Ass?
options: A poor makeshift of a team
The finest team in the district
A team that worked in perfect harmony
A team the Ploughman had used for years

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Ass say about the day they've had?
options: That it was a hard day
That it went by too quickly
That it was easier than usual
That the master was unfair to them

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what exact answer does the Ox give to the Ass's question?
options: "You, to be sure, as usual"
"Neither of us should have to"
"I will carry him tonight instead"
"Let us ask the master himself"

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the word "usual" in the Ox's reply suggest about carrying the master?
options: It is a task that regularly falls to the Ass, not something new
It is a task the Ox performs most days
It happens only on days when they plough together
It is a task the master normally does himself

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "makeshift" mean in "a poor makeshift of a team"?
options: A temporary substitute used because nothing better is available
A prize-winning arrangement
A team trained specially for racing
A pair of animals of the same species

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: After a day of ploughing together, the Ass asks who will carry the master home, and the Ox says it is the Ass's job as usual
The Ox refuses to plough alongside the Ass any longer
The Ploughman decides to buy a second Ox after the day's work
The Ass and Ox argue over who worked harder during the ploughing
